TASK: clear the accumulated lint debt and do an accessibility/responsive pass on the public-facing pages.

## The lint debt
`npx eslint app lib components` currently reports exactly 12 errors, all pre-existing, in these files:
- `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx` (5)
- `components/marketing/HeroMock.tsx` (2)
- `components/marketing/FeatureVisuals.tsx` (1)
- `components/marketing/ThemeToggle.tsx` (1)
- `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` (1)
- `app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx` (1)
- `app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx` (1)

They are mostly `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` and `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`.

**Fix them properly, do not silence them.** A `// eslint-disable` line is acceptable ONLY where the rule is genuinely wrong for that case AND you write a comment explaining precisely why — and say so in your report. Blanket-disabling is a failure of this task.

Important on `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`: the usual correct fix is to derive state during render, use `useSyncExternalStore` for genuinely external state (theme, media queries, browser feature detection), or lazy-initialise. Read the rule's reasoning before reaching for a disable. **Several of these guard against hydration mismatch** — read the surrounding code carefully and DO NOT reintroduce a hydration error while fixing a lint warning. The owner has already been bitten by a hydration bug in this app once; causing another would be a real regression.

The `any` in PromptHero is a SpeechRecognition shim — the Web Speech API has no DOM lib types in TypeScript. A minimal hand-written interface is the right fix.

## The accessibility / responsive pass
On the public pages ONLY (`app/(auth)/**`, `app/pricing/**`, `app/contact/**`, `app/page.tsx`, `components/marketing/**`):
- Keyboard: everything interactive reachable and operable, visible `:focus-visible` state, no keyboard traps, sensible tab order.
- Semantics: real landmarks, one `<h1>` per page, headings not skipping levels, buttons vs links used correctly (a thing that navigates is a link), form inputs with real associated labels, images with appropriate alt text (decorative ones `alt=""`).
- Contrast: check text against its actual background in BOTH light and dark themes. This app has a `.dark` class-based theme — check both.
- Motion: the app has several animations (see `app/globals.css`). Verify `prefers-reduced-motion` is genuinely honoured.
- Responsive: no horizontal body scroll at 380px wide. The system prompt for generated sites targets 380px; the marketing site should meet its own bar.

Fix what you find. Where a fix would be a visual redesign rather than an accessibility fix, report it instead of doing it.

## Scope — you may edit ONLY:
`components/marketing/**`, `app/(auth)/**`, `app/pricing/**`, `app/contact/**`, `app/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`

## Critical constraints
- DO NOT modify: `app/globals.css` (owned by someone else — if you need a CSS change, report it instead), `app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx`, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/projects/**, app/settings/**, app/admin/**, app/legal/**, prisma/schema.prisma, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- DO NOT add npm dependencies. (framer-motion, lucide-react and tailwind are already present — check package.json for what you may use.)
- DO NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **Do not change visual design.** This is a correctness pass. Colours, layout and copy stay as they are unless a contrast failure forces a minimal adjustment — and flag every such change in your report.
- `PromptHero.tsx` was recently modified to add an "Enhance" feature and `app/(auth)/**` has a password show/hide toggle. Read files fresh before editing; preserve that behaviour.
- There is a dev server on http://localhost:3003 you can use. **Note: the Browser pane may not composite frames, so CSS animation `currentTime` can read as 0 and screenshots may time out — verify computed styles and DOM structure programmatically rather than relying on screenshots.**
- End state must be: `npx eslint app lib components` reports ZERO errors, and `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Report back
Each lint error and how you fixed it (or why you disabled it), every accessibility issue found and whether you fixed it, any contrast adjustment you made, and anything you found but deliberately left alone.

No hydration errors on a fresh load of `/`, `/pricing`, `/contact`, `/login`, `/signup` (including `/signup?error=google_failed`). **Zero `eslint-disable` lines added.** ## Lint debt — all 12, fixed at the source **`PromptHero.tsx` (5)** - 4× `no-explicit-any`: replaced with a hand-written Web Speech shim — `SpeechRecognitionEventLike` / `ResultLike` / `AlternativeLike` / `SpeechRecognitionCtor`, covering exactly the members used. `window` is narrowed locally via `window as unknown as SpeechCapableWindow` rather than `declare global`, so it can't collide if TS's DOM lib ever ships these types. - `set-state-in-effect` (`setSpeechSupported`): → `useSyncExternalStore(NEVER_CHANGES, readSpeechSupported, () => false)`. This is the textbook case — browser feature detection is external state, unknowable on the server. `getServerSnapshot` feeds both SSR and the hydration render, so the mic button still stays out of the server HTML. **Hydration guard preserved.** **`HeroMock.tsx` (2)** — restructured so state resets by *remount*, React's own reset mechanism, instead of by effect: - l.47 (typewriter `setCount(0)` when inactive): extracted `TypingPanel`, mounted only during the typing phase. `useTypewriter` lost its `active` param and its reset entirely. - l.114 (`setBookingStep("browse")` on `liveCycle`): extracted `LivePanel`, which owns `bookingStep` and is mounted only during the live phase — `useState("browse")` runs fresh each entry. This also let me delete `liveCycle`, which removed an impure `setLiveCycle` call nested inside a `setPhase` updater. Verified in-browser over 22s: browse → Booked+toast → back to browse on each cycle, identical to before. - Also extracted `BuildingEllipsis` so its 400ms interval only runs during the building phase. **`ThemeToggle.tsx` (1)** — `useSyncExternalStore` with a `MutationObserver` on ``. `getServerSnapshot` returns `null`, exactly reproducing the old "render nothing until we know" hydration guard against the inline no-flash script in `layout.tsx`. Bonus: the icon now follows class changes made by anything else, and the toggle no longer needs to mirror state. **`login/page.tsx` + `signup/page.tsx` (2)** — the effect did two things: - sessionStorage read → new shared `components/marketing/usePendingPrompt.ts` using `useSyncExternalStore` with `getServerSnapshot = () => null`. **Hydration guard preserved** — the "picking up where you left off" panel still never appears in server HTML. - `?error=` → derived during render: lazy `useState` initializer plus React's documented "adjust state when a prop changes" render-time comparison for later client navigations. Verified no hydration warning with `?error=` in the URL. **`FeatureVisuals.tsx` (1)** — `jsx-no-comment-textnodes`: the `//` really is content, so it's now `{"// real .tsx, …"}`. **`TopUpButton.tsx` (1)** — `react-hooks/immutability` on `window.location.href = url` → `window.location.assign(url)`. Same navigation, method call instead of a host-object mutation. ## Accessibility — found and fixed **Keyboard** - `PasswordInput`'s show/hide toggle had `tabIndex={-1}` — mouse-only. Now a normal tab stop with `aria-pressed`. (Show/hide behaviour preserved.) - `MotionLift` (`FloatCard.tsx`) rendered a **phantom `
`** around every submit button on login, signup and contact — framer-motion adds it for `whileTap`. Nameless, roleless, did nothing. Verified absent from the tab order. - Mobile menu had no way out from the keyboard → Escape now closes it and returns focus to the toggle.
